gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named reviewer's measured scan accuracy for any scanner in these combos. The only one found is Notebookcheck's test of the Creality Sermoon S1, whose maker claims 0.02 mm: the reviewer measured 0.02–0.04 mm on a reference ball, under 0.30 mm on most flat faces, 0.50–0.60 mm on depth detail and a 0.24 mm height error on a printed part.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited Creality pages (the Scanner Combo collection and the K2 Plus combo page), which list no specs or measurements at all. I also checked 3dprintmates, which gives only unattributed spec-sheet figures and says it checked 'published specs', and rottenwifi, which gives only maker or listing figures and says 'promotional specifications are not a substitute for independent accuracy testing'. The Notebookcheck item at rank 6 is a paid placement about the Sermoon P1 that repeats Creality's 'up to 0.02 mm under laboratory conditions' with no testing. None of them has a measured deviation for any scanner.
decides: The only named lab measurement found shows a $2,399 Creality scanner coming out 2 to 30 times less accurate than its 0.02 mm claim on real features, depending on the feature. That makes the 0.05–0.1 mm claims on the cheaper combo scanners (Otter Lite, Ferret SE, Moose Lite) best-case figures, not part-copying tolerances. For a shopper scanning replacement parts, it supports buying the scanner and printer separately and planning to correct key dimensions in CAD with calipers. It is not a reason to pay more for an 'all-in-one' bundle. It does not rank the budget combos against each other, because none of them has a named measurement.

findings.label: Measured accuracy, scanned 3D-printed part (glue stick)
findings.value: hole depth off 0.03 mm, diameter off 0.04 mm, height off 0.24 mm
findings.source_title: Creality Sermoon S1 3D scanner review: Precision for everyday engineering (Notebookcheck, Vineet Washington)
findings.note: The print had a 0.2 mm brim layer, which may explain most of the 0.24 mm height error. This is the closest test to the shopper's scan-a-part-and-reprint use.

findings.label: Measured scan speed
findings.value: up to 57 fps blue laser and 30 fps infrared over USB to an M4 MacBook Air; 45 and 20 fps wireless via Scan Bridge
findings.source_title: Creality Sermoon S1 3D scanner review: Precision for everyday engineering (Notebookcheck, Vineet Washington)
findings.note: Creality's spec is up to 70 fps (34 cross lines) and 90 fps (7 parallel lines or single line). Measured blue-laser speed is 81% of the 70 fps claim (57/70).

findings.label: Measured scan-to-print workflow time
findings.value: initial scan under 10 min; process-ready scan under 20 min; plus 5–7 min fusion and meshing on a MacBook Air; mouse stand scanned to printed prototype in under 30 min
findings.source_title: Creality Sermoon S1 3D scanner review: Precision for everyday engineering (Notebookcheck, Vineet Washington)
findings.note: The 30-minute scan-to-print figure is for a small part. The page gives no noise or power measurement; it says only that the fan is 'audible but not loud'.
